mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-increase period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for three consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as reducing risk aversion, which amplifies equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 96,000 and remains below for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during the three months prior to the labor strength signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) exceeding 0.5% of prior month's PCE suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected corporate profits and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly log growth rate exceeds +0.5%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 5-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production by more than 2% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, which can reduce production costs and improve margins, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly log decline exceeds -2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during the two months prior to the supply easing signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for a month, the market anticipates a near-term rate hike, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% in a month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period with <3% inflation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) above 240,000 indicate labor market weakness that increases perceived risk, lowering equity valuations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 240,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the two months prior to the labor stress signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time monthly surge in retail sales (not captured in GDPC1 but proxyable via external series if available) above 2% of the prior month's value suggests unanticipated demand, prompting market optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly log growth rate exceeds +2%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 5-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) shows three consecutive months of flat or declining growth (<0.1% monthly), market participants anticipate supply constraints, prompting a premium on safe assets and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly log growth rate remains ≤ 0.1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the three-month pre-stagnation period (p > 0.05).
